subdomain: 6.1 Conduct structured discovery and requirement gathering

en.question: A railway proposes using Claude to draft inspection reports. The sponsor wants maintenance decisions made sooner, but only report-writing time has been measured. Engineers must still verify findings and authorize work. What should discovery establish before selecting an architecture?

options.text: The fastest model configuration for producing reports of the current average length, using the existing report template.
options.note: Generation speed addresses one stage, not the sponsor's elapsed time to an authorized maintenance decision.

options.text: The current path to an authorized decision, its delays and rework, affected roles, and consequences of incorrect findings.
options.note: This establishes the outcome baseline, workflow boundaries, and error costs against which a proposed solution can be assessed.

options.text: The annual inspection volume multiplied by the demonstrated reduction in drafting time, treated as the expected decision-time improvement.
options.note: Drafting-time savings do not establish the effect of verification queues, rework, or authorization on decision time.

options.text: The reporting features preferred by engineering managers, ranked before examining the verification and authorization stages of the workflow.
options.note: Manager preferences are useful inputs but cannot replace discovery of the stages that determine the stated business outcome.
